An engineer had been building from his own interpretation rather than the backlog story, then writing tests after the code. The backlog was also part of the problem: stories lacked defined scenarios and a definition of done.

Instead of treating this only as an individual engineer’s mistake, Matt changed the work around the team. He rebuilt the backlog with SMART, testable stories and brought frontend and backend test-driven development experts from Columbus to work side by side with the engineers. They redid the code and test cases using an “I do, we do, you do” progression, supported by boot camps, coding katas, practice learning sessions, and lunch and learns.

He also restructured agile ceremonies to keep stakeholders, developers, and product managers aligned, and delivered product management and SMART story training.

Defect rates dropped as story quality and test-first discipline took hold. The client stopped finding defects the dashboard could not see, and confidence was restored through the open audit and visible improvement.
